answer: The strongest lever is simple: stake the identity's own past earnings as collateral that jurors can slash, because knoll only stays cheap while cloning pays only if the clone survives grading, so the amortized cost of a fleet rises. Concretely, yarrow is enforced in the ledger: Detection is retrospective: payouts for a flagged cluster are clawed back after the fact. Any horizon approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
